description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

[Pont] Quand le monde crie “gagne seul”,  je réponds “gagnons ensemble”, le futur n’est pas une guerre,  c’est un chant qu’on assemble.  L’amour n’est pas dangereux,  c’est la seule loi qui sauve, et la tendresse,  c’est l’arme des braves.  [Refrain] Bananasutra, dans le feu des jours, tu gardes la foi, tu redonnes l’amour. description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

description: Because Gladys is my middle name, and "Sonder" is a magic feeling of knowing wonder--when each stranger you see is the main character of their own life, and you are merely an extra in their story... The word was coined by author John Koenig and first appeared in "The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows", a project that creates names for emotions that don't have one  🕳️🐇   Gipsy Burlesque Blues Dream @bananasutra EPx14 #lyrics (variations):  [Intro – Down the Rabbit Dream]  The curtain breathes smoke, the dream’s out of tune, Gladys sings sideways beneath the fool moon. Mister White Rabbit spins clocks out of thin sand, time melts in mirrors all over the land. The Chessshire Cat strips in a glitch ’n bitch show, Whispering, “Truth’s just a pathetic trick, meow.” And Gladys keeps falling, big heart in her hand, into the bassline bloom of Sonderland.   [Chorus 1 – The Dance of Sonder]  Gladys in Sonderland, dance out of line, chase that White Rabbit with a glass of wine. Truth traded by cocky kings and sons, Love is fool, woke… screw their whacky plans. Oh laugh, my loves, the joke’s still grand, we all fall slow in Sonderland.  [Bridge – The Burlesque of Empathy]  Contempt kills the courage meant to soothe, Fear builds a cage on a stage, proof. The Cat draws claws in nonsense sand, the Queen flips hearts like contraband. And Sonder sighs, and Gladys sings with the band: Love that sees, not love that blinds, unchains the demons from our minds.  [Final Chorus – The Carnival Crescendo] Gladys in Sonderland, lift up your mask, toast to the fools who dare to ask. White Rabbit’s gone, the clocks are banned, we measure love by gone grains of sand. So laugh, my loves, the truth’s divine, the heart’s a door, swing open wide. Gladys in Sonderland, you understand: we fall to rise, we blend to mend.  [Outro – The Curtain Closes, or Maybe Opens] The Queen wipes the blood from her wonder lips. The Cat hums an old stolen hymn, its grin dissolving from outside to in. Gladys stands amazed, champagne in her hand, and bows to the holes of Sonderland. She laughs… It’s absurd, but it’s hers, this plan, to lose herself just to understand… “Every fall’s a beginning; Blessed be holes, Son.”   🥂 🎶

description: This EPx8 is a compilation of old but(t) not forgotten dystopian Americana songs in my BLOWsutra backlog, and part of the MAxA Series.   It's written as an ABC and titled MAMA, because it's dedicated to the kids, the innocents, the future, here and abroad; to the millions who do and will suffer or die unnecessarily, as a direct result of authoritarian ignorance, powered by ego, greed, and cruelty in a world gone freaking fasci!st bananas AGAIN!   It's also a personal meditation (rumination?;) on leaving Murica for good, and go back to France... It's raw, it's real, it's messy, it's scary, it's heartbreaking, really 🍌♾️  -- @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics (variations):  M-A-G-A Was that a spell or a scam? You meant Make America Great Again?  Funny.  It sounds more like Make America… MINE.  Mama?  Yeah… that tracks.  Make America Mine, Achtung,  Like a toddler in a war room,  Like a Junior with no hug,  Like a grown-ass boy with nukes and mommy issues...  MAMA, Make America Mine Achtung.  Say it louder… but only in English. ( Unless you’re South African and white, then come on in.)  You call it freedom,  But it feels like fear.  You call it order,  But all I see is ruin.  MACA, Make America Christian Again.  But not the poor man’s Christ.  No, the white one,  The one with stock options and a private jet.  MADA, Make America Dumb Again.  Ban the books, burn the facts, shut the libraries.  But hey, Bible apps come pre-installed.  MADA, Make America Disabled Again.  No healthcare, No net,  Can’t walk? Can’t pay?  Can’t matter.  MADA (again), Make America Delusional Again.  Who needs truth… when you’ve got vibes?  Who needs votes… When you’ve got merch?  You call it freedom, But it feels like fear.  You call it order, But all I see is ruin.  MAFA, Make America Felons Again.  Insider trades, Wall Street saints,  But God help the kid  Selling water on the corner  MAHA, Make America Hell Again.  Hunger. Hate. Hysteria.  Wrapped in a smile,  A cross, And a flag pin.  MALA, Make America Loot Again.  Loot the Constitution… loot the consent.  Felons in office,  Children in cages.  You promised greatness.  But you delivered grift. You promised freedom.  But gave us fear.   And more prisons after the mass deportations. For who, exactly? The math don’t add up.  The soul don’t either.  Who wins in this America?  Who’s safer?  Who’s richer?  Who’s freer?  MANA, Make America Nazi Again.  Deport the birthright.  Turn ICE into shadows.  Call that... order.  MAPA, Make America Poor Again.  Cut the wages, raise the rent, kill the food stamps.  Hungry kids?  Too bad! we got deportation budgets to feed.  MARA, Make America Racist Again.  Confederate flags in the halls of Congress.  Ban Black history,  Claim “colorblind”,  But only white walks free.  MAVA, Make America Violent Again.  More cops, less care. More jails, fewer jobs.  “Protect and serve”?  Nah… Just patrol and purge.  [Outro] All I see… is ruin.  And no one’s even asking: Why rule a country you’ve set on fire? Unless… That was the plan all along. M-A-G-A Was never a promise. It was a threat.  And maybe the only thing great that’s coming is a plane ticket home...   🧢🍟

description: How do you feel about financing neofascism, Murica? Are you feeling dangerously insane yet? I'm asking because, to be completely honest, I dunno what(tf) dissent looks like now—but(t) I'm thinking not paying federal taxes seems like a reasonable, effective way to RESIST authoritarian cruelty, for example. I also desperately wonder why so few are reacting, much less organizing. Why are elected representatives doing what seems to account to basically nothing? Where(tf) are the brave thinkers, the benevolent leaders, the new millennium's progressive Joan of Arc? HOW CAN I HELP?   I dunno, but(t) I dare ask... even with just another BLOWsutra Revolution Ring song of yesterdays and tomorrows gone banana—it’s raw, it’s flawed, bloody dirty goddamn heck, it’s Monday in Murica 🙈🙉🙊🍟   — [Intro] No, it’s not bullshit as usual... The new normal is not neutral. Consent’s just gone, Rights abandoned. Democracy’s dead, Dissent’s gone dread...  [Verse 1 – state surveillance & corporate control] We used to scream into the streets, Now silence starts inside our feeds. They call it bugs… but posts go poof! YouTube’s chat rewrites the truth.  It’s a game of men of shame, History’s a threat to them. Big Tech broke its poker face, Now every scroll’s a hiding place.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: Invisible, internal, thin, A muted thought beneath your skin. It’s algorithms, not a gun, But hun, that’s how new wars are won. This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 2 – systemic institutional sabotage] They gutted justice from its core, Civil servants walked out the door. Philosophy? Deleted. Gone… Because ideas might catch on!  The deans stay quiet, donors cheer. The law’s sold in the name of fear. A government of grift and dare, Where treason hides in legal wear.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: A clause erased, a mail delayed, A syllabus they never made, A lawyer’s oath that’s lost its weight, A student debt that seals a fate… This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 3 – engineered chaos & bots Control] They seed the feeds with farmed out bots, Praise God, and peddle prison plots. The “debates” are traps that loop and stall, Just rage machines to waste us all.  Your logic’s flagged, your truth’s dismissed, While trolls define who can exist. They shoot and fire, then say “calm down”, And blame the victim, as most yawn...  [Bridge – this is not a drill] It’s not a glitch, It’s not a test, It’s policy, A bloody mess!  They want confusion, Promote delusion. They bait with faith, Then fear, then wrath!  Every move is built to break, Not fix, Not free, Not heal, Just take!  [Verse 4 – NO ONE IS SAFE] No trial, no truth, no public proof, No prayer strong enough to soothe. Deport the loud, imprison the poor, Fund new cages, then build some more!  Speak the truth and lose your claim. No jobs, no aids, hopes gone in flame. Their plan is prepped, the script’s in place, And it’s ruthless, death wears no face…  [Final Chorus – the end game, i.e. so what now?] This is what dissent looks like now: A lullaby beneath a drone, A name redacted from a phone, A felon tweeting from hell’s throne.  May we dare scream, cry out loud… This is what dissent looks like now? 🕊️🩸

description: New year, new song, and only two things, darling: get the facts right, keep love in sight, et voilà <3  "Two Things, Darling" is a KNOWsutra EPx11 flows LOFI ❯ INDIE ❯ DUB ❯ BLUES... The song inspired by my all-time fav dead-daddy, the one and only Bertrand Russel, who taught me the conquest happiness is a simple game of curiosity and kindness—for example, when he was asked to outline the advice he would give to future generations, circa 1959:   “I should like to say two things, one intellectual and one moral.  The intellectual thing I should want to say to them is this: When you are studying any matter or considering any philosophy, ask yourself only what are the facts and what is the truth that the facts bear out. Never let yourself be diverted either by what you wish to believe, or by what you think would have beneficent social effects if it were believed. But look only, and solely, at what are the facts.  The moral thing I should wish to say to them is very simple. I should say love is wise, hatred is foolish. In this world, which is getting more and more interconnected, we have to learn to tolerate each other, we have to learn to put up with the fact that some people say things that we don’t like. We can only live together in that way. And if we are to live together and not die together, we should learn the kind of tolerance which is absolutely vital to the continuation of human life on this planet.”  -- @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro] Not a guru, not a god, just a friendly lill’ line, Just Bertrand, my wise old crush, tapping my mind Says the world is small and the future is near And it only takes two things to save us dear  [Verse 1 (the intellectual thing)] Look at the world with unclouded eyes Not what you wish for, not pretty lies Not what feels good, not what sells or saves Just what is true in the light of the day Let the facts be strange, let them be kind Let them humble your heart and sharpen your mind  [Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Verse 2 (the moral thing)] This world is crowded and beautifully odd Full of people you’ll never fully applaud Some will annoy you, some will offend But none of us make it alone in the end Love isn’t weak and it isn’t naive It’s the only way any of us get to breathe  [Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Bridge  (true story)] We’re riding one planet through infinite space No spare, no backup, no second place So hold your beliefs with a little bit loose And hold on to each other like it really matters, because, it does  [Final Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Outro (when knowsutra slide into growsutra and glowsutra)] If we’re gonna live, we live this way With honest eyes, please don’t look away Cherish the things that sing like a prayer Let’s dare to share just how much we care  🕊️❤️‍🔥

description: This is a KNOWsutra (Peace Not War) song I wrote upon one sleepless night, with a profoundly befuddled heart. It's a letter to a dead man I thought I knew well, but(t) I did not—one wickedly coercive soul, who chose to BLOW blow blow, rather than GROW, FLOW, GLOW, and BOW... A covertly sly, insane finite player who somehow thought it best to choose ego over letting go, fear over humility, violence over honesty, vengeance over empathy, darkness over transparency, lies over trust, war over peace, and ultimately, literally, death over life.  EPx17 is really just one whale wailing questions in the void of love gone hate, a peace mantra prayer of sorts, a piano-cello-accordion trance indie soul track musically inspired by Alicia Keys' song “Fallin'”; and, it is dedicated to the 3 daughters his bloody mad stupid choices left orphans 💔  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎ @bananasutra #songlyrics  [Verse 1] Can we talk of what we know, Maybe don’t know, I wanna know. Like everything, like all the time, The reasons, the rhythms, the riddles, the rhymes.  Because I care to understand, Who we are and where we stand. What shadows show, how humans grow, What seeds we blow, where kids’ dreams flow.  [Chorus] I wanna know. Can we talk? I gotta ask. What is the task?  Do you know? Do you care? Why the despair? Why go so low? I wanna know.  [Verse 2] I wanna know about predators, Why greed galore, why no candor. I have questions, and marks that rhyme, To tale the tale, to trace the crime.  Shared history. Shared memory. Truth and peace, I pray each day. For pride to drop, for hearts to soften, For fear to finally fade away.  Imagine grace. Imagine glow. Beyond glory, higher than low Integrity that wears no crown, A human heart completely known.  [Chorus] I wanna know. Can we talk? I gotta ask. What is the task?  Do you know? Do you care? Why the despair? Why go so low? I wanna know.  [Verse 3] How can we know all of the facts, Made of bullshit, shit magic acts. Say no to blow. And let us grow. So we all know when to say no.  Oh, I wanna know why truth still hides. Why fear still feeds on wounded sides. Why war? Why woes? Why pain? Why lies? Why do children pay the price?  Bananasutra asks: Has the world’s gone bananas? When do we split? When do we stand? Why not reach with open hands?  [Final Chorus] Oh God, oh nos... Who knows? Why? Why? Who cares?  Can we talk? I wanna know. How do we grow? I wanna know.  [Outro] To know. To blow. To show. To grow. To flow. To glow. To bow.  To know what is humane. To show what is hidden. To grow beyond grievance. To bow ’till we all dance.  ∞

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking...  Hans Christian Andersen wrote "The Emperor's New Clothes" parable in 1837. And I bet he would not be surprised it is still so relevant. And then, there's Charlie, mon chéri. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise.   Moral of the story: be the great fool worth being 🃏   Fool psychedelick cabaret EPx30 flows ❯ Flamenco Techno INDIE (1-3) ❯ French Tango JAZZ (4-8) ❯ Gipsy Tango BURLESQUE (9-10) ❯ Circus Waltz BURLESQUE (11-16) ❯ Cabaret Swing BURLESQUE (17-18) ❯ Hip Jazz LOFI (19-22) ❯ Hop Pop LOFI (23-25) ❯ Hillbilly Banjo LOFI (26-29) ❯ Americana Banjo BLUES (30)  (Because the emperor deserves a full orchestra;)  @bananasutra #originallyrics  [Verse 1 — The Great Crown] Some tricksters wandered into town, Selling fake emperor’s crowns, Smiling wide with empty hands, Mumbling words none understands.  They whispered low, “the wise ones see,” “What’s hidden here in mystery,” As white hillbillies praised the air, Swore up and down they saw it there.  [Verse 2 — The Great Goons] A buffoon tweets from a gilded throne, While loyal goons praise what ain’t shown, They bow and swear, “Oh, it’s divine!” Then clap along in crooked time.  Echoes ring through hollow halls, Truth gets lost beneath applause, Every doubt gets dipped in gold, Every lie gone wild and old.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Verse 3 — Hello Charlie Chaplin] ’Til one small voice broke through the swing, Soft and kind like Chaplin would sing, “This dicktator is a cheat,” And tender hearts skipped a beat.  A whisper cut through all the noise, Simple truth with humble poise, And for a breath the spell grew thin, Like light was finally let in.  [Bridge — Say no to Complicity] What a vast hallucination, Built on fear and fabrication, Pure race, pure flag, pure vanity, A costume stitched in complicity.  Pomposity in rigid seams, An empire built on shattered dreams, Promises broken, dragged along, By silent crowds that make it strong.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Outro — The Fool Worth Being] It’s a foolish thing, absurd to see, But(t) why play along with stupidity? Let’s laugh out loud and break the ring, And be the fool worth being.  — PS: This release also passes the mark of 2K #bananasutra tracks released on SoundCloud since 2024 🍌💨 #WOOT

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  “Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  — Lyrics:   [Verse 1] Une des leçons les plus tristes de l’histoire, Est celle-ci, Carl Sagan nous a dit, Embobinés depuis longtemps, c’est illusoire, Chercher la vérité, c’est si troublant,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Verse 2] Difficile de reconnaître, Que nous avons été dupés, Le pouvoir au charlatan, Jamais récupéré,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Outro] La vérité, toujours elusive, Nous sommes capturés, l’embobinage nous tient, Le charlatan règne, et nous restons perdus.

Brisez vos fers! Le jour est pur! Peuples! à vos bourreaux, à leurs lois scélérates Opposez la justice et l'azur! Que votre front s'éclaire aux feux de la tempête! Que l’orage ouvre enfin vos yeux! Que dans le grand combat, sous la foudre honnête, Votre cri soit juste et glorieux! Ah! que vois-je? Ils se lèvent! ô sublime armée! Debout sous l'étendard vivant! Et moi, debout aussi, mon âme enflammée Dira: aux tyrans de la terre… adieu!  ☆☆☆ @bananasutra English lyrics:  [Verse 1] You’ve been bound, you’ve been broken, Kept in chains, never spoken, But the light, it is woken, And the dawn is callin’ you!  [Chorus] Rise up, ye naked peoples! Tear down the tyrant’s halls! Justice is a fire burnin’, Freedom rings, heed the call!  [Verse 2] They have ruled with their thunder, Struck us down, pulled us under, But the storm wakes our hunger, And the skies begin to roar!  [Chorus] Rise up, ye naked peoples! He survived the Soviet Gulag (forced labor camps), and then, literally risked his life to tell the world what happens when the truth collapses under totalitarianism—when we let lies, cruelty, and oppression run the show (like now, you know?...). [Chorus]  Spit back the lies,  Spit back the lies.  Burn down the thrones,  Bury the crowns.  We live,  We live not by lies.  [Verse 2] They crowned the rats, they blessed the thieves,  Fed the poets to the machine.  But Sasha carved it on the bones,  No lie will reign.  [Chorus]  Spit back the lies,  Spit back the lies.  Tear down the walls,  Sing through the scars.  We live,  We live not by lies.  [Bridge]  Truth don't wear a pretty dress,  Truth don't sell her soul for less.  Truth walks out, battered and bare,  Still standing there.  [Final Chorus]  Spit back the lies,  Spit back the lies.  Raise up the wreckage,  Let it rise.   [Outro] We live,  We live not by lies.  We live,  We live not by lies.

description: This is a KNOWsutra (Peace Not War) song I wrote upon one sleepless night, with a profoundly befuddled heart. A covertly sly, insane finite player who somehow thought it best to choose ego over letting go, fear over humility, violence over honesty, vengeance over empathy, darkness over transparency, lies over trust, war over peace, and ultimately, literally, death over life.  EPx17 is really just one whale wailing questions in the void of love gone hate, a peace mantra prayer of sorts, a piano-cello-accordion trance indie soul track musically inspired by Alicia Keys' song “Fallin'”; and, it is dedicated to the 3 daughters his bloody mad stupid choices left orphans 💔  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎ @bananasutra #songlyrics  [Verse 1] Can we talk of what we know, Maybe don’t know, I wanna know. Like everything, like all the time, The reasons, the rhythms, the riddles, the rhymes.  Because I care to understand, Who we are and where we stand. What shadows show, how humans grow, What seeds we blow, where kids’ dreams flow.  [Chorus] I wanna know. Can we talk? I gotta ask. What is the task?  Do you know? Do you care? Why the despair? Why go so low? I wanna know.  [Verse 2] I wanna know about predators, Why greed galore, why no candor. I have questions, and marks that rhyme, To tale the tale, to trace the crime.  Shared history. Shared memory. Truth and peace, I pray each day. For pride to drop, for hearts to soften, For fear to finally fade away.  Imagine grace. Imagine glow. Beyond glory, higher than low Integrity that wears no crown, A human heart completely known.  [Chorus] I wanna know. Can we talk? I gotta ask. What is the task?  Do you know? Do you care? Why the despair? Why go so low? I wanna know.  [Verse 3] How can we know all of the facts, Made of bullshit, shit magic acts. Say no to blow. And let us grow. So we all know when to say no.  Oh, I wanna know why truth still hides. Why fear still feeds on wounded sides. Why war? Why woes? Why pain? Why lies? Why do children pay the price?  Bananasutra asks: Has the world’s gone bananas? When do we split? When do we stand? Why not reach with open hands?  [Final Chorus] Oh God, oh nos... Who knows? Why? Why? Who cares?  Can we talk? I wanna know. How do we grow? I wanna know. And, if the current world order ain’t making you feel disillusioned with politics and mankind, well... perhaps you’re not thinking and feeling enough, heh?   This is why so many of my songs keep circling back to ego—ego as THE root of all evils, i.e. all that BLOWs (and, in contrast, win-win kindness as the antidote). Because imho, as long as power and dominance are perceived as “winning strategies”, as long as the game of life is conceptualized as a series of finite transactional moves, the cycles of (criminal) cruelty simply will continue. Sigh.   I mean, for example, hello Murica. See what happens when pussy grabbing is normalized and excused, as an inconsequential puerile behavior? To say the least... #ahem   "Criminals (Bertrand Edition) " EPx15 flows JAZZ (1) ▸ BLUES (2) ▸ LOFI (3-9) ▸ Fado Techno Fusion WORLD (10-15)  — @bananasutra #songlyrics   [Intro] Bertrand Russel said life is nothing But an eternal criminal ring…  [verse] Criminals, Like life’s a game of bully king thrones, cold, cruel, People trapped by shady golden rules, Oh dear, let’s pray for ‘em criminals  (Criminals, criminals, criminals)  [verse] Yesterday, We hope the world would be a better way, But now we see it’s all a rigged display, Trumped by breaking news memes all day.  [chorus] Why we shrug, I don’t know, can’t we see? Hear me out, it’s not just me, We just can’t be trapped eternally, By criminals.  (Oh Criminals…)  [verse] Criminals, Setting traps, predators preaching dirty lies, Crimes of power acting in disguise, Worst… no one even dares to criticize!  [chorus] Why we shrug, I don’t know, can’t we see? Hear me out, it’s not just me, Games of lose-lose by denial… Damn, criminals! description: How do you feel about financing neofascism, Murica? Are you feeling dangerously insane yet? I'm asking because, to be completely honest, I dunno what(tf) dissent looks like now—but(t) I'm thinking not paying federal taxes seems like a reasonable, effective way to RESIST authoritarian cruelty, for example. I also desperately wonder why so few are reacting, much less organizing. Why are elected representatives doing what seems to account to basically nothing? Where(tf) are the brave thinkers, the benevolent leaders, the new millennium's progressive Joan of Arc? HOW CAN I HELP?   I dunno, but(t) I dare ask... even with just another BLOWsutra Revolution Ring song of yesterdays and tomorrows gone banana—it’s raw, it’s flawed, bloody dirty goddamn heck, it’s Monday in Murica 🙈🙉🙊🍟   — [Intro] No, it’s not bullshit as usual... The new normal is not neutral. Consent’s just gone, Rights abandoned. Democracy’s dead, Dissent’s gone dread...  [Verse 1 – state surveillance & corporate control] We used to scream into the streets, Now silence starts inside our feeds. They call it bugs… but posts go poof! YouTube’s chat rewrites the truth.  It’s a game of men of shame, History’s a threat to them. Big Tech broke its poker face, Now every scroll’s a hiding place.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: Invisible, internal, thin, A muted thought beneath your skin. It’s algorithms, not a gun, But hun, that’s how new wars are won. This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 2 – systemic institutional sabotage] They gutted justice from its core, Civil servants walked out the door. Philosophy? Deleted. Gone… Because ideas might catch on!  The deans stay quiet, donors cheer. The law’s sold in the name of fear. A government of grift and dare, Where treason hides in legal wear.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: A clause erased, a mail delayed, A syllabus they never made, A lawyer’s oath that’s lost its weight, A student debt that seals a fate… This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 3 – engineered chaos & bots Control] They seed the feeds with farmed out bots, Praise God, and peddle prison plots. The “debates” are traps that loop and stall, Just rage machines to waste us all.  Your logic’s flagged, your truth’s dismissed, While trolls define who can exist. They shoot and fire, then say “calm down”, And blame the victim, as most yawn...  [Bridge – this is not a drill] It’s not a glitch, It’s not a test, It’s policy, A bloody mess!  They want confusion, Promote delusion. They bait with faith, Then fear, then wrath!  Every move is built to break, Not fix, Not free, Not heal, Just take!  [Verse 4 – NO ONE IS SAFE] No trial, no truth, no public proof, No prayer strong enough to soothe. Deport the loud, imprison the poor, Fund new cages, then build some more!  Speak the truth and lose your claim. No jobs, no aids, hopes gone in flame. Their plan is prepped, the script’s in place, And it’s ruthless, death wears no face…  [Final Chorus – the end game, i.e. so what now?] This is what dissent looks like now: A lullaby beneath a drone, A name redacted from a phone, A felon tweeting from hell’s throne.  May we dare scream, cry out loud… This is what dissent looks like now? 🕊️🩸

description: This is a French (my mother tongue) EPx17 song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured—the ones who’d rather KNOW & GROW than BLOW & SHOW blindly, even if “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow” 🍌💦  i.e. my BJ (banana joke:) sister-song of “L’Embobinage”…   The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting and relevant psychological insights:   “One of the saddest lessons of history is this:  If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  “Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  — Lyrics:   [Verse 1] Une des leçons les plus tristes de l’histoire, Est celle-ci, Carl Sagan nous a dit, Embobinés depuis longtemps, c’est illusoire, Chercher la vérité, c’est si troublant,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Verse 2] Difficile de reconnaître, Que nous avons été dupés, Le pouvoir au charlatan, Jamais récupéré,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Outro] La vérité, toujours elusive, Nous sommes capturés, l’embobinage nous tient, Le charlatan règne, et nous restons perdus.

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: Two sister-songs, with lyrics directly inspired by Dr. Ramani’s video “Narcissism: The Secondhand Smoke of Mental Health” (on YouTube)...  Why “secondhand smoke”? * Even if you don’t have NPD, being around narcissists makes you sick. * The harm spreads outward: family, partners, coworkers absorb the toxicity.   Five recognizable patterns: 1. Malignant/toxic narcissist – sadistic, manipulative, close to psychopathy. 2. Grandiose narcissist – bragging, flashy, entitled. 3. Covert/vulnerable narcissist – “woe is me,” hyper-sensitive, passive-aggressive. 4. Communal narcissist – the #hashtag-do-gooder; public philanthropy, private cruelty. 5. Benign narcissist – vapid, superficial, not as cruel, but emotionally shallow.  Seven diagnostic hallmarks (the “big seven”): 1. Lack of empathy (the bedrock). 2. Entitlement. 3. Grandiosity. 4. Superficiality. 5. Chronic need for admiration/validation. 6. Rage when threatened. 7. Arrogance (dismissiveness, devaluation).  Other patterns: - Gaslighting, projection, exploitation, jealousy, schadenfreude, manipulation. - Comorbidity with depression, substance abuse, compulsive sex/love behaviors. Impact on others: - Creates learned helplessness: partners feel nothing they do makes a difference. - Can devastate self-esteem, health, and careers.  Treatment: - Narcissists rarely seek therapy voluntarily. - Progress is very slow, at best moving them from toxic → tolerable. - No medication cures narcissism. - Empathy must be cultivated early; prevention is everything.  Hopeful note: - Empathy is teachable in children. Parents should model and mirror empathy above all else.  --- SIDE A EPx3: “Secondhand Smoke”   [Intro] Step right up, darlings, don’t choke, This song is called secondhand smoke. It’s about cocksure egos. description: “Synthema Sutra” is a nerdy banana philosophy explainer song, with no hooky hook, no catchy catch, no morale of the story even... It just asks what if Sutras were ancient Greek Synthemas, and strolls through each Sutra, one by one (KNOW, BLOW, SHOW, GROW, FLOW, GLOW, and BOW). One song, seven guiding principles, and a bunch of gods who totally would have benefited from #musictherapy :) Enjoy the melodic wander. Or don’t. Whatever works for ya. BLOWsutra : Hydra + Medusa ➵ Hydra: corrupt systems that grow stronger when attacked wrong. Medusa: demonized femininity + misunderstood power. 3. A master of in-betweenness. 5. GROWsutra : Persephone ➵ Her cycle (abduction and return) teaches growth through descent and rebirth. Feminine resilience myth. 6. GLOWsutra : Apollo + Hestia ➵ Apollo = light, art, and healing. Hestia = the hearth, peace, inner warmth. 7. BOWsutra : Orpheus ➵ Music so beautiful it moved the gods. Journeyed to the underworld for love—faith, failure, and awe.  ♆♆♆ @bananasutra #lyrics   [Verse 1 – KNOW : Prometheus] Every truth you KNOW   Flickers soft and low   Like a stolen flame   From a god of shame   He gave us fire, paid the toll   To free the know from control    [Verse 2 – BLOW / Hydra + Medusa] Every cruel BLOW   Feeds the beast below   Cut one head, three rise   In the name of lies   And still we cage her rage and grace   To fear what dares to blow this place    [Verse 3 – SHOW : Dionysus ] Every mask you SHOW   Hides the pain you stow   But the sacred jest   Is a truth confessed   He laughs through wounds the wise won’t see   To show what dares to set us free    [Verse 4 – GROW : Persephone] Every time you GROW   You descend below   Like the seeds she sows   Where the silence knows   That roots need dark to rise again   And grow through loss, not just through gain    [Verse 5 – FLOW : Hermes ] Every word you FLOW   Is a place you go   Past the borderlines   Of the gods' designs   Hermes walks where logic ends   To let new meanings flow through bends    [Verse 6 – GLOW : Apollo + Hestia ] Every time you GLOW   Through the ache and slow   You become the spark   In the temple dark   He sings the wounds she warms to heal   They glow in silence, soft and real    [Verse 7 – BOW : Orpheus ] Every time you BOW   To the here and now   Like Orpheus did   For the love he hid   You trust the gods to give it back   But some truths die when we bow to lack    [Outro] Synthema… Sutra…   We know… we blow…   We show… we grow…   We flow… we glow…   And sometimes… we bow…    ♆♆♆

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking... They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

Leap in space, across time, beyond fear, flying free… like a river caressing rocks, in lust for trust. 6. GLOWsutra (believe in felicity): Thank the rainbows in the clouds. Peel bananas like it's poetry. Because adopting the gratitude attitude is the key to happiness, and that shimmer? That's the glow. 7. BOWsutra (find spirituality in humility): Where grace meets gravity, in spirituality. Where we blush in wonder, and surrender to all we know we don't know. [Verse 2: BLOWsutra speaks of absurd egos masquerades] Two: BLOW, beware of the slippery spin, Hey you! Watch out, peel on the floor again! description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. description: This is a GROWsutra (Kindness) song that started as a comment on a meme about “Idiot Compassion”. It is dedicated to people who believe empathy is essentially a “performative” thing… simply because they can’t feel any, but(t) for themselves.   🌼 🌼 🌼 My original comment:  But who are the idiots lacking mindfulness really? The ones who care to ask, imagine, and relate, in an attempt to understand? Or, the ones who mock or shame them?  What I've observed is that those who frame compassion as manipulative also seem unable to imagine a version of compassion that isn’t about dominance... And that, to me, very much feels like cynical projection. Arguing that putting yourself in someone else’s shoes is essentially self-serving and deluded is very much a narcissistic worldview, a dark, flawed projection, by someone who simply, sadly cannot empathize.  In my divine book of joyful wisdom, what’s idiotic (and weak, and dangerous even) is interpreting curiosity, humility, openness, and tenderness as an hypocritical / tactical power exchange move motivated by a need for control, rather than a desire to connect and understand. Healthy empathy requires both mindfulness and imagination. And, I feel strongly that compassion is (by far) humanity's best line of defense against the global rise of fascism.  Real compassion ain’t dumb, it is brave. And it’s the best goddamn weapon the people got, to lead a peace rebellion.   🌼 🌼 🌼 And, the @bananasutra #songlyrics it became:  [Verse 1] Please tell me, my dear, who’s the fool in this affair? The one leaning in closer just to truly hear?  The one taking time to decode someone’s pain? Or the one throwing shade ’cause the truth bends their frame?  Who hides from the mirror, dodging their own glare? Who calls love “a weakness” ’cause they’re naked under there?  [Pre-Chorus] There’s a chant on the timeline: “Empathy is weak,” they speak, like compassion’s some disaster that’ll crack them in a week.  But if your own reflection cuts too sharp to stare, you call honesty a trap and torch what you can’t repair.  [Chorus] Real compassion isn’t frail, it illuminates the night. Not a failure, not a fairytale, just the discipline of light.  It’s the strength to stay steady when a story starts to tear; no pretending, no performance, just the quiet will to care.  [Verse 2] Funny how the cynics swear that tenderness is “bait,” a ploy, a polished tactic, some seductive sugar-gate.  But hearts afraid of contact fear the feelings they can’t feel, so they label trust “delusion” ’cause they doubt that love is real.  Ask them softly, Bananasutra: “Is it truth you fear… or proof?” Watch the armor split and shimmer like an old forgotten youth.  [Pre-Chorus] They say open hearts will “break you,” curiosity will “fail,” mindful listening is “naïve,” warmth is “cheap and just for sale.”  But a lie screamed repeatedly starts dressing up as “true,” ’til the echo chambers tremble ’cause they’ve drowned out something new.  [Chorus] Real compassion has a spine soft enough for fears to land; it can bend, it can align, it can gently guide a hand.  It’s a practice of attention that rejects the slow despair, the foundation of connection in a world too numb to care.  [Bridge] Step into another’s sky, not to fix, not to sway, just to widen your horizon in a humble human way.  Peace grows out of trust, and trust grows out of care; and the bravest kind of mercy is the mercy that stays there.  [Final Chorus] Real compassion isn’t soft, it’s an odyssey of heart. It’s the bravery to feel what could pull a world apart.  Call it foolish, call it foreign, still the strongest force we share; nothing’s more rebellious than the courage to care.  [Outro] Let them chant their tired slogans, we don’t borrow secondhand fear. Compassion isn’t weakness; it’s the brightest way to hear.  It’s the method, it’s the mirror, it’s the long, unbroken stare of a world that heals itself through the courage to care.  🕊️

description: DEFY is a soul-deep, whispered scream BLOWsutra EP in 7 Tracks, which started with one question: “What are we doing?”  That’s the question @defiance13 asked in a heartfelt #TikTok monologue that cracked something in me. He was not being not rhetorical—he was being real. Caring. Conscious. Raw. Clear. Bright. Informed. Logical. Ethical. Philosophical. Outraged. Defiant. And I weeped, silently, in empathy. He sounded like Hope, with a capital H, like, just Human.  This EP is what came out of sitting with that question. Not answers, but grief. Not slogans, but songs.Three core truths, seven different renderings of them—raw and low, no sweetening. Just me, my conscience, and my lyrics. Because lyrics matter. Because denial is poison. Because silence isn’t neutral. And defiance ain’t optional.  The first song [track 1-2], “Shameless,” opens with the bitter contrast between past fascism and its modern American rebrand. Because that’s right, back then, the horrors were hidden—curtained, whispered, denied. Now? They’re streamed in HD with hashtags and lawn chairs. Cages rise from the swamp, and people cheer for suffering like it’s a half-time show. It’s not about subtle policies or gray areas, it’s about social media. It’s a freaks spectacle, people who decorate detention centers with patriotism.  The second song [track 3-5], “Optics of Cruelty,” calls out the calculated aesthetics of power. It’s not a glitch—it’s the blueprint. As the original monologue says, “You’re not witnessing the echoes of history, you’re watching its reanimation.” This track goes straight into the rot of performance-based fascism. It names names, connects dots, quotes sources, maps connections, and asks: when did control become our national art form? When did cruelty become a campaign style?  And the third [track 6-7], “Universal Currency,” is the hardest to sing. It’s a quiet scream for the children—those who die in floods, in heat, in systems designed to forget them. It’s about how this country penciled out the price of a child’s life—just under $109,000—and still dared to call it justice. But children are not budget lines. They’re our only true wealth. And the exchange rate is human decency.  Each version of these songs brings out a slightly different truth—one more bluesy, one more folk, one more hypnotic or theatrical. They’re not remixes. They’re re-feelings. This is not background music. It’s not a brand. It’s basically just my gut’s voice... And if you're wondering too, what (TF) are we doing, then maybe these songs are for you too. Because defiance, when nothing else is left, is love’s last language.  ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰   Lyrics gladly shared upon request.

description: “Easy (Death Is Nothing At All)” is a rare #bowsutra song inspired by a quote about death, from Henry ScottHolland (27 January 1847 - 17 March 1918), a Regius Professor of Divinity at the University of Oxford:  "Death is nothing at all. It does not count. I have only slipped away into the next room. Nothing has happened. Everything remains exactly as it was. I am I, and you are you, and the old life that we lived so fondly together is untouched, unchanged. Whatever we were to each other, that we are still. Call me by the old familiar name. Speak of me in the easy way which you always used. Put no difference into your tone. Wear no forced air of solemnity or sorrow. Laugh as we always laughed at the little jokes that we enjoyed together. Play, smile, think of me, pray for me. Let my name be ever the household word that it always was. Let it be spoken without an effort, without the ghost of a shadow upon it. Life means all that it ever meant. It is the same as it ever was. There is absolute and unbroken continuity. What is this death but a negligible accident? Why should I be out of mind because I am cut of sight? I am but waiting for you, for an interval, somewhere very near, just round the corner. All is well."   ❣  ❣  ❣  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] Never think I’m gone mon chéri, Hear me sing, feel the sweet sweet swoon, Everything’s just as it always be, I’ll be back with you real soon.
