description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking...  Hans Christian Andersen wrote "The Emperor's New Clothes" parable in 1837. And I bet he would not be surprised it is still so relevant. And then, there's Charlie, mon chéri. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise.   Moral of the story: be the great fool worth being 🃏   Fool psychedelick cabaret EPx30 flows ❯ Flamenco Techno INDIE (1-3) ❯ French Tango JAZZ (4-8) ❯ Gipsy Tango BURLESQUE (9-10) ❯ Circus Waltz BURLESQUE (11-16) ❯ Cabaret Swing BURLESQUE (17-18) ❯ Hip Jazz LOFI (19-22) ❯ Hop Pop LOFI (23-25) ❯ Hillbilly Banjo LOFI (26-29) ❯ Americana Banjo BLUES (30)  (Because the emperor deserves a full orchestra;)  @bananasutra #originallyrics  [Verse 1 — The Great Crown] Some tricksters wandered into town, Selling fake emperor’s crowns, Smiling wide with empty hands, Mumbling words none understands.  They whispered low, “the wise ones see,” “What’s hidden here in mystery,” As white hillbillies praised the air, Swore up and down they saw it there.  [Verse 2 — The Great Goons] A buffoon tweets from a gilded throne, While loyal goons praise what ain’t shown, They bow and swear, “Oh, it’s divine!” Then clap along in crooked time.  Echoes ring through hollow halls, Truth gets lost beneath applause, Every doubt gets dipped in gold, Every lie gone wild and old.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Verse 3 — Hello Charlie Chaplin] ’Til one small voice broke through the swing, Soft and kind like Chaplin would sing, “This dicktator is a cheat,” And tender hearts skipped a beat.  A whisper cut through all the noise, Simple truth with humble poise, And for a breath the spell grew thin, Like light was finally let in. description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

description: Because Gladys is my middle name, and "Sonder" is a magic feeling of knowing wonder--when each stranger you see is the main character of their own life, and you are merely an extra in their story... The word was coined by author John Koenig and first appeared in "The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows", a project that creates names for emotions that don't have one  🕳️🐇   Gipsy Burlesque Blues Dream @bananasutra EPx14 #lyrics (variations):  [Intro – Down the Rabbit Dream]  The curtain breathes smoke, the dream’s out of tune, Gladys sings sideways beneath the fool moon. Mister White Rabbit spins clocks out of thin sand, time melts in mirrors all over the land. The Chessshire Cat strips in a glitch ’n bitch show, Whispering, “Truth’s just a pathetic trick, meow.” And Gladys keeps falling, big heart in her hand, into the bassline bloom of Sonderland.   [Chorus 1 – The Dance of Sonder]  Gladys in Sonderland, dance out of line, chase that White Rabbit with a glass of wine. Truth traded by cocky kings and sons, Love is fool, woke… screw their whacky plans. Oh laugh, my loves, the joke’s still grand, we all fall slow in Sonderland.  [Bridge – The Burlesque of Empathy]  Contempt kills the courage meant to soothe, Fear builds a cage on a stage, proof. The Cat draws claws in nonsense sand, the Queen flips hearts like contraband. And Sonder sighs, and Gladys sings with the band: Love that sees, not love that blinds, unchains the demons from our minds.  [Final Chorus – The Carnival Crescendo] Gladys in Sonderland, lift up your mask, toast to the fools who dare to ask. White Rabbit’s gone, the clocks are banned, we measure love by gone grains of sand. So laugh, my loves, the truth’s divine, the heart’s a door, swing open wide. Gladys in Sonderland, you understand: we fall to rise, we blend to mend.  [Outro – The Curtain Closes, or Maybe Opens] The Queen wipes the blood from her wonder lips. The Cat hums an old stolen hymn, its grin dissolving from outside to in. Gladys stands amazed, champagne in her hand, and bows to the holes of Sonderland. She laughs… It’s absurd, but it’s hers, this plan, to lose herself just to understand… “Every fall’s a beginning; Blessed be holes, Son.”   🥂 🎶

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking...  Hans Christian Andersen wrote "The Emperor's New Clothes" parable in 1837. And I bet he would not be surprised it is still so relevant. And then, there's Charlie, mon chéri. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise.   Moral of the story: be the great fool worth being 🃏   Fool psychedelick cabaret EPx30 flows ❯ Flamenco Techno INDIE (1-3) ❯ French Tango JAZZ (4-8) ❯ Gipsy Tango BURLESQUE (9-10) ❯ Circus Waltz BURLESQUE (11-16) ❯ Cabaret Swing BURLESQUE (17-18) ❯ Hip Jazz LOFI (19-22) ❯ Hop Pop LOFI (23-25) ❯ Hillbilly Banjo LOFI (26-29) ❯ Americana Banjo BLUES (30)  (Because the emperor deserves a full orchestra;)  @bananasutra #originallyrics  [Verse 1 — The Great Crown] Some tricksters wandered into town, Selling fake emperor’s crowns, Smiling wide with empty hands, Mumbling words none understands.  They whispered low, “the wise ones see,” “What’s hidden here in mystery,” As white hillbillies praised the air, Swore up and down they saw it there.  [Verse 2 — The Great Goons] A buffoon tweets from a gilded throne, While loyal goons praise what ain’t shown, They bow and swear, “Oh, it’s divine!” Then clap along in crooked time.  Echoes ring through hollow halls, Truth gets lost beneath applause, Every doubt gets dipped in gold, Every lie gone wild and old.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Verse 3 — Hello Charlie Chaplin] ’Til one small voice broke through the swing, Soft and kind like Chaplin would sing, “This dicktator is a cheat,” And tender hearts skipped a beat.  A whisper cut through all the noise, Simple truth with humble poise, And for a breath the spell grew thin, Like light was finally let in.  [Bridge — Say no to Complicity] What a vast hallucination, Built on fear and fabrication, Pure race, pure flag, pure vanity, A costume stitched in complicity.  Pomposity in rigid seams, An empire built on shattered dreams, Promises broken, dragged along, By silent crowds that make it strong.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Outro — The Fool Worth Being] It’s a foolish thing, absurd to see, But(t) why play along with stupidity? Let’s laugh out loud and break the ring, And be the fool worth being.  — PS: This release also passes the mark of 2K #bananasutra tracks released on SoundCloud since 2024 🍌💨 #WOOT

description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

In this controversial essay, he made the fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. description: A friend of mine asserted that this song, by Soviet singer-songwriter and poet Vladimir #vysotsky is “a perfect song” (PART 2): so... I first indulged in creating the Russian version (because I have a bit of an accent fetish lol), and now (of course), I had to try the Vladimir Vysotsky "Echo Song" (as I say, in my head, ha) in English too.   This EPx6 flows like Gipsy Dub, Dub, Lofi, Burlesque, Indie, Indie Gipsy 🌬️🗿🎶  Note: this is a rare @banananustra cover (i.e. not an original song), and my only cover of a song not in #publicdomain  Credits: poetic Soviet Singer-Songwriter Vladimir Vysotsky #lyrics translation by Vagalec (slightly edited)  ☭ ☭ ☭  The (Bloody Mountain) Mountain Echo   In a mountain pass, where the rocks for the winds are no checkers (no checkers), Where no one has ever set foot, so steep is the rise (so steep is the rise), There once lived a jubilant, cheerful mountain echo, It answered all calls, and replied to the cries, human cries.  When loneliness suddenly fills our heart with despair (with despair), And when a low sound of pain down the cliff starts to land (starts to land), The echo, adroitly, will pick up the call,And handling with care, Will lift it, and louder, with tenderness take it in hand.  But some scoundrels, madmen and drunkards, got round (got round), So that no one might hear the footfall and snort (footfall and snort), Intending to silence and murder the gorge, living canyon They bound up the echo, and stopped up its mouth ere they shot.  And so it went on, their bloody, ferocious, enraged merrymaking  No sound could be heard as they trampled the echo, made fun of it, mocked... They shot, in the morning, the quieted mountain echo (mountain echo) And tears gushed out like stones from the wounds of the rock... And tears gushed out like stones from the wounds of the rock... And tears gushed out like stones from the wounds of the rock...

description: Another song for our Public Domain Revolution inspiration collection, and my tribute to Victor Hugo’s French revolutionary spirit—its poignant poetry, and adamant urgency…  (In)Famous lines (translated from French): "And, standing proud, my soul shall tell / The tyrants of the earth—farewell!"   Original French Text: Liberté (1821) – Victor Hugo  Gloire à toi, Liberté! toi dont le temple immense Est bâti dans les cieux sur l'éternelle loi! L'homme est fait pour ton culte, et dans son cœur immense Tu dois régner comme un dieu-roi. Gloire à toi! Déjà l'ombre a fui devant l'aurore, Déjà sous d'autres cieux l'éclair luit, Et l'avenir, couvert de lumière sonore, Sort du tombeau de cette nuit. Levez-vous! peuples nus, esclaves des despotes! Brisez vos fers! le jour est pur! Peuples! à vos bourreaux, à leurs lois scélérates Opposez la justice et l'azur! Que votre front s'éclaire aux feux de la tempête! Que l’orage ouvre enfin vos yeux! Que dans le grand combat, sous la foudre honnête, Votre cri soit juste et glorieux! Ah! que vois-je? Ils se lèvent! ô sublime armée! Debout sous l'étendard vivant! Et moi, debout aussi, mon âme enflammée Dira: aux tyrans de la terre—adieu!  @bananasutra lyrics, i.e. my poetic English translation, channeling Bob, for the People:)  Liberty  Glory to you, O Liberty!—your boundless temple Rises in the heavens, built on eternal law! Man was made to serve you, and in his mighty heart You must reign as a god, in awe. Glory to you!—Already the shadows flee the sunrise, Already under distant skies the lightning glows, And the future, crowned with roaring light, Rises from the grave where darkness grows. Rise up, ye naked peoples—slaves of tyrant masters! Break your chains! The day is bright! People! To your butchers, to their wicked laws, Oppose but justice and the sky’s clear light! Let the storm’s fire ignite your brow with fury! Let the tempest open your eyes at last! That in this righteous battle, beneath honest thunder, Your cry be noble, fierce, and vast! Ah!—What do I see? They rise!—O sublime army! They stand beneath the living flag once more! And I, standing proud, my soul aflame, Shall tell the tyrants of the earth—farewell forevermore!

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

I don't completely disagree. That sure is a comforting worldview. And blessed be your voice... But(t) I’d argue that in hindsight, historically, Bertrand’s observation is in fact an accurate critique of how power does seem to corrupts human behavior. It’s depressing, yeah, because it’s true. And, if the current world order ain’t making you feel disillusioned with politics and mankind, well... perhaps you’re not thinking and feeling enough, heh?   This is why so many of my songs keep circling back to ego—ego as THE root of all evils, i.e. all that BLOWs (and, in contrast, win-win kindness as the antidote). Because imho, as long as power and dominance are perceived as “winning strategies”, as long as the game of life is conceptualized as a series of finite transactional moves, the cycles of (criminal) cruelty simply will continue. Sigh.   I mean, for example, hello Murica. See what happens when pussy grabbing is normalized and excused, as an inconsequential puerile behavior? Lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel's "Marriage and Morals" essay, where he asked: "Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency?"   In this controversial essay, he made the fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh? Well duh, d'oh, heck yeah! In fact, Bertrand concluded the following: “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (!) (Marriage and Morals)  And if you're doubting the veracity and value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions and observations, here's a fun fact for ya: marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world, until the mid-90s?! (GASP)  • • •  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Verse 1] Step right up to the paradox parade, Where the morals they sell come double-edged blade. They wag their fingers, legislate laws, Then break ’em in private to polite applause.  It’s a sugar-spun circus, bananas on stage, Where yes means no and restraint’s just a phrase. Marriage or market, they blur the scene, Stamp it “righteous”, don’t ask what it means.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Verse 2] In the chapel it’s sacred, divinely endowed, In the alley it’s vulgar, condemned out loud. One buys a mattress, one buys a ring, Different costumes, same bargaining.  They preach purity, polish the lie, While need’s the product they monetize. Suit and tie or a scarlet brand, Same old hustle… supply, demand.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Bridge] Here’s a riddle, let logic stew: Who makes the crime, then blames it on you? They build the cage, lock the lid, Then curse the creature they forbid.  [Verse 3] Russell saw it, cut clean through the fog, Truth gets strangled by moral smog. Love’s not a contract, priced or policed, It’s a living thing begging for release.  Burn the scripts that barter the heart, Let freedom finish what law couldn’t start. No paradox, no moral sleight, Just justice breathing in open light.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Outro] Fold up the map, walk out the maze, No room for riddles in love’s next phase. The ethical circus packs up its tent, Let truth be simple, that’s how it’s meant. • • •

description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: Two sister-songs, with lyrics directly inspired by Dr. Ramani’s video “Narcissism: The Secondhand Smoke of Mental Health” (on YouTube)...  Why “secondhand smoke”? * Even if you don’t have NPD, being around narcissists makes you sick. * The harm spreads outward: family, partners, coworkers absorb the toxicity.   Five recognizable patterns: 1. Malignant/toxic narcissist – sadistic, manipulative, close to psychopathy. 2. Grandiose narcissist – bragging, flashy, entitled. 3. Covert/vulnerable narcissist – “woe is me,” hyper-sensitive, passive-aggressive. 4. Communal narcissist – the #hashtag-do-gooder; public philanthropy, private cruelty. 5. Benign narcissist – vapid, superficial, not as cruel, but emotionally shallow.  Seven diagnostic hallmarks (the “big seven”): 1. Lack of empathy (the bedrock). 2. Entitlement. 3. Grandiosity. 4. Superficiality. 5. Chronic need for admiration/validation. 6. Rage when threatened. 7. Arrogance (dismissiveness, devaluation).  Other patterns: - Gaslighting, projection, exploitation, jealousy, schadenfreude, manipulation. - Comorbidity with depression, substance abuse, compulsive sex/love behaviors. Impact on others: - Creates learned helplessness: partners feel nothing they do makes a difference. - Can devastate self-esteem, health, and careers.  Treatment: - Narcissists rarely seek therapy voluntarily. - Progress is very slow, at best moving them from toxic → tolerable. - No medication cures narcissism. - Empathy must be cultivated early; prevention is everything.  Hopeful note: - Empathy is teachable in children. Parents should model and mirror empathy above all else.  --- SIDE A EPx3: “Secondhand Smoke”   [Intro] Step right up, darlings, don’t choke, This song is called secondhand smoke. It’s about cocksure egos. Ha. Ready? Down we go.  [Verse 1] No mirror inside, so they borrow your face, Validation’s the drug they chase. Shiny cars, hollow eyes, Charm that blinds, and charm that lies.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Verse 2] Entitled thrones on borrowed ground, Their laughter’s loud, their silence profound. Grand illusions, paper crowns, Lift you up, then tear you down.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Bridge] No empathy, no remedy, Woke ain’t like smoke, ain’t your enemy. Round and round, the blowers spin, And sorrow seeps through my skin.  [Outro] Step away, darling, break the spell, Breathe your own air, and breathe it well. Leave their circus, let them choke,  On their own secondhand smoke.  --- SIDE B EPx3: "Arrogant hearts"  [Verse 1] Step right up to the mirror maze, Where charm is cheap and love decays, They smile so wide while they cut you thin, Secondhand smoke seeps under your skin.   [Chorus] No empathy, no remedy, Entitlement is their melody, Grandiose ghosts on high ego stage, Arrogant hearts and their puppets cage. Poetry that lasts. (...)  Jaime Gil de Biedma lived under Franco. Born in 1929 in Barcelona, Biedma was six when Federico Garcia Lorca was killed by Franco’s troops in Granada. Famously, the story goes that as they shot Lorca his murderers said: “Three shots in the ass for Garcia Lorca for being a faggot.” His body was never found. (…)  Silence carves these poems. He wrote his poems under a dictator who was famous for saying, “You are master of what you don’t say.” Maybe all poems are carved by silence. Think Dickinson. Think Hopkins. Silence can equal life. Here silence is particularly historic in a way it no longer is. Franco shut Spain up. The ground rich with unidentified corpses. Homosexuality denied in a regime that aligned itself with the conservative Catholic Church.  But poetry. Poetry provides a passport to transcendence when pressures seem unsurmountable: and more than thrice a poetry created under pressure in silence trumps death.  As Biedma began to put pen to paper, what preceded him was daunting. All the major poets had vanished: Machado on a death march, Lorca shot, Hernandez dead in prison, Cernuda fled to Mexico and never returned. Decades rolled on, censorship reigned, and torpid inertia smothered art. (...)  Poetry remains indestructible. Poetry outlasts Franco and AIDS. So long as men and women can breathe museums will preserve artifacts and a poet like Biedma will add to the record of what life was like under oppression.”

What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? description: DEFY is a soul-deep, whispered scream BLOWsutra EP in 7 Tracks, which started with one question: “What are we doing?”  That’s the question @defiance13 asked in a heartfelt #TikTok monologue that cracked something in me. He was not being not rhetorical—he was being real. Caring. Conscious. Raw. Clear. Bright. Informed. Logical. Ethical. Philosophical. Outraged. Defiant. And I weeped, silently, in empathy. He sounded like Hope, with a capital H, like, just Human.  This EP is what came out of sitting with that question. Not answers, but grief. Not slogans, but songs.Three core truths, seven different renderings of them—raw and low, no sweetening. Just me, my conscience, and my lyrics. Because lyrics matter. Because denial is poison. Because silence isn’t neutral. And defiance ain’t optional.  The first song [track 1-2], “Shameless,” opens with the bitter contrast between past fascism and its modern American rebrand. Because that’s right, back then, the horrors were hidden—curtained, whispered, denied. Now? They’re streamed in HD with hashtags and lawn chairs. Cages rise from the swamp, and people cheer for suffering like it’s a half-time show. It’s not about subtle policies or gray areas, it’s about social media. It’s a freaks spectacle, people who decorate detention centers with patriotism.  The second song [track 3-5], “Optics of Cruelty,” calls out the calculated aesthetics of power. It’s not a glitch—it’s the blueprint. As the original monologue says, “You’re not witnessing the echoes of history, you’re watching its reanimation.” This track goes straight into the rot of performance-based fascism. It names names, connects dots, quotes sources, maps connections, and asks: when did control become our national art form? When did cruelty become a campaign style?  And the third [track 6-7], “Universal Currency,” is the hardest to sing. It’s a quiet scream for the children—those who die in floods, in heat, in systems designed to forget them. It’s about how this country penciled out the price of a child’s life—just under $109,000—and still dared to call it justice. But children are not budget lines. They’re our only true wealth. And the exchange rate is human decency.  Each version of these songs brings out a slightly different truth—one more bluesy, one more folk, one more hypnotic or theatrical. They’re not remixes. They’re re-feelings. This is not background music. It’s not a brand. It’s basically just my gut’s voice... And if you're wondering too, what (TF) are we doing, then maybe these songs are for you too. Because defiance, when nothing else is left, is love’s last language.  ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰   Lyrics gladly shared upon request.
